newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mercosur ministers tie up Bolivian free trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Mercosur ministers tie up Bolivian free trade pact.

text.p: Foreign and economy ministers of South America's Mercosur trading bloc paved the way for the signing of a free trade agreement with Bolivia, the second country in the region to join the group this year.
Pending approval of the parliaments of the four Mercosur member countries, Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, the Bolivian free trade agreement should come into effect in April 1997.
Bolivia is the second country to forge ties with Mercosur, Latin America's fastest-growing trade block, after Chile reached a similar agreement earlier this year.
"We are very proud the Bolivian free trade agreement was completed in the period in which Brazil chaired the negotiations," said Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia.

Negotiations between Bolivia and the Mercosur partners almost broke down this week when Argentina objected to several items which the Bolivians had included on a list of products that would fall outside the pact.
The Mercosur partners also agreed on a common set of rules under which they would be entitled to resort to trade safeguards that would protect them against dumping practices.
The agreement is central to the future of Mercosur, currently a customs union which is slowly working towards a tighter integration framework along the lines of the European Union common market.
Among other issues, the ministers also approved a model for the new Mercosur logo which will show four stars of the Southern Cross constellation.
The new logo will be used on exports produced in the four countries and it is hoped it will become a distinguishing band of quality and competition.
On Tuesday the four Mercosur presidents will meet for talks with the presidents of Chile and Bolivia and to sign the Bolivian free trade agreement.
